declaration.unit: UTC day; all matched windows including zero-fill windows
declaration.null: paired policy difference has zero mean and symmetric whole-day effects; all 512 day sign flips
declaration.multiplicity: max absolute studentized statistic over original 10 variants x J/X
declaration.confidence_interval: paired day t interval, df=8; exploratory and unadjusted
declaration.carry_control: scale v1 inventory per day to CAP10 market-implied binary variance q^2*m60*(1-m60); ex-post diagnostic, not an executable policy
declaration.limitation: CAP10 was already selected on these consumed days. This is not out-of-sample validation; multiplicity screen omits earlier searches.
controls: all baseline windows match round i
identical/opposed paired effects exercise sign-flip checker

interpretation_limits: CAP10 suppresses inventory-increasing quotes at known absolute inventory >= 10; it is not a hard inventory cap or compulsory unwind.

All nine days were consumed before this audit; ten variants and two timing assumptions had already been examined. Neither the day intervals nor sign-flip diagnostic validates a selected policy out of sample.
Post-stop marks value the fixed residual position; they are not executable exits and include no unwind costs.
Near-expiry marks carry forward the last valid book. Their age is reported below; late mark P&L cannot independently validate settlement alpha.
Risk-matched carry uses an ex-post market-mid binary variance proxy, not an executable sizing rule or a demonstrated directional prediction advantage.
Settlement labels are the saved venue resolution outcomes used by the engine; this audit reconciles that accounting, not the external oracle itself.
